profile.name: Soumya Roy
profile.tagline: Machine learning researcher working on model reliability, interpretability, and evaluation — especially in large language models.
profile.summary: I work at the boundary of rigorous mathematics and modern deep learning. My clinical and behavioural health research spans ICU vital sign monitoring, cervical cancer risk prediction, and student depression risk, using SHAP-based stratification and custom imputation to keep models explainable beyond clean benchmarks. More recently I have been working across modern AI systems : large language models, retrieval augmented generation, vision language models, and agentic pipelines where models plan, check, and revise each other. What ties this together is a refusal to take a model's output at face value. I want to know which data shaped it, why it behaves the way it does, and where it quietly fails.
profile.goal: Next stop: a fully-funded PhD in machine learning or AI, most likely in data attribution, interpretability, or agentic systems. Long term, I'm aiming for a research career and, eventually, a professorship.

publications.title: Membership or Understanding? What the Imitation Game Measures When the Respondent Is a Language Model
publications.description: A solo-authored examination of what the Imitation Game actually measures when the respondent is a language model, separating group membership cues from genuine understanding.

publications.title: Explainable Early Prediction of Acute Hypotensive Episodes in ICU Patients Using Routine Vital Signs: An eICU Study
publications.description: Early-warning model for acute hypotensive episodes in ICU patients, built on routine vital signs with an emphasis on clinical interpretability over raw predictive accuracy.

publications.title: Machine Learning-Based Risk Factor Analysis for Cervical Cancer Prediction: A Comparative Study of Class Imbalance Handling Strategies with SHAP-Driven Clinical Risk Stratification
publications.description: Comparative evaluation of class imbalance strategies for cervical cancer risk prediction, paired with SHAP-driven stratification to keep risk attribution transparent and clinically usable.

publications.title: Local Bounded Stochastic Imputation for Ordered Numerical Sequences
publications.description: A bounded stochastic imputation method for ordered numerical sequences, designed to preserve local structure in incomplete real-world data without introducing unbounded noise.

publications.title: A Mathematical Index for Quantifying and Reducing Student Depression Risk Through Personalised Behavioural Guidance
publications.description: A quantitative index for student depression risk that supports personalised, behaviourally grounded guidance rather than a single opaque score.

llm.title: IMDB Sentiment: Exact Leave-One-Out Data Attribution
llm.description: Exact Leave-One-Out data attribution for sentiment classification: retrains a logistic regression model 800 times, once per training point removed, to measure each review's true causal effect on test log loss. Built on a stratified 1,000-review sample from the deduplicated 49,582-row IMDB dataset with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings. Baseline accuracy 0.80, log loss 0.4594. Influence scores cluster near zero, but the extremes are informative: harmful points tend to be sarcastic or ambiguous reviews mislabelled relative to their sentiment, while helpful points are clear-cut and strongly worded. A direct look at why exact attribution doesn't scale, and why approximations like Shapley values and influence functions exist.

llm.title: LLM Quantization from First Principles
llm.description: Per-tensor vs per-channel INT8 quantization implemented from scratch in PyTorch on Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, deliberately avoiding bitsandbytes, GPTQ, AWQ, and GGUF to understand why per-channel wins rather than just that it does. Row-by-row outlier analysis found max/mean ratios from 3.2x on uniform channels up to 16x on outlier-heavy ones. Per-channel scaling cut average quantization error by 93.86%, and normalisation weights proved an order of magnitude more sensitive than Linear layers, so they were kept in FP16. Perplexity on WikiText-2: FP16 18.7963, per-tensor 19.6739, per-channel 18.7606.

llm.title: Quantization Tradeoffs in LLMs
llm.description: Measuring what you actually gain and lose when quantizing: FP16, INT8, and INT4 (NF4) benchmarked on Qwen2.5-0.5B for memory, perplexity, and inference speed. INT8 gave a 36% memory cut for a 0.08% perplexity increase, essentially free; INT4 gave 54% for 6.25%. The surprise was speed: INT8 was the slowest configuration tested, likely per-operation overhead in the LLM.int8() kernel on single-sequence generation, while INT4 ran ~70% faster than FP16. A reminder that quantization method matters as much as bit-width, and that tradeoff curves should be measured rather than assumed.

llm.title: Human vs AI Medical Answer Similarity
llm.description: How close are AI-generated medical answers to real doctors' answers? Sampled 50 Q&A pairs from the HC3 medicine corpus, generated matched Llama 3.3 70B responses, embedded both with all-MiniLM-L6-v2, and compared cosine similarity (mean 0.578). Length explained only ~11% of the variance, so filtering for long-but-dissimilar pairs isolated the real pattern: humans ask clarifying questions, admit uncertainty, and name specific drugs, doses, and specialists, while the AI commits to a full answer regardless and defaults to 'consult a doctor' as a closing move.

llm.title: GPTQ INT8 Quantization: Cross-Model Comparison
llm.description: Applies GPTQ's Hessian-guided, error-compensated INT8 quantization via the GPTQModel library to two architecturally different models, Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct and SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct, to test whether quality preservation holds across architectures rather than just one model family. Calibration and evaluation data were drawn from separate WikiText-2 splits and tokenized per-model to avoid leakage. Perplexity barely moved for either model: Qwen went from 12.3246 to 12.3352, SmolLM2 from 11.4971 to 11.4960, changes small enough to be noise. The consistency across two different architectures, not just one, was the core question this project set out to answer.

llm.title: GPT-2 Quantization Reconstruction Error
llm.description: A from-scratch 4-bit, per-channel, symmetric quantization function applied to every weight-bearing layer of GPT-2 small (49 Linear and Conv1D layers), measuring not weight error but output error: the MSE between each layer's real activations and its quantized counterpart's, captured via forward hooks on identical calibration input from ag_news. Error compounds with depth, early blocks (0-5) mostly stay under 1.0 MSE, later blocks climb sharply, peaking at transformer.h.11.attn.c_proj (17.4 MSE), with output projection (c_proj) layers consistently the most sensitive. lm_head was the outlier by far, at 1891.56 MSE, over 100x any other layer, which is why many real-world pipelines keep the output layer at higher precision while compressing the rest aggressively.

agents.title: Cross-Model Critique Agent
agents.description: A LangChain (LCEL) pipeline testing whether one model can catch another's errors better than it can catch its own. Llama 3.1 8B answers a logic puzzle, Llama 3.3 70B critiques the reasoning without solving it independently, then the first model revises or defends its answer. Pairing two different models is deliberate: a model critiquing itself tends to agree with itself. Correctness is judged live by the user, building a session scoreboard that tracks accuracy and how often the answer actually changed after critique.

agents.title: AI Debate Arena
agents.description: Two Groq-hosted language models debate a topic you give them, one arguing for and one against, with arguments streaming turn-by-turn through a LangGraph state machine. The user judges the winner. Built to explore how adversarial framing between two agents surfaces reasoning that a single model tends to smooth over.

agents.title: LangGraph Breaking News Assistant
agents.description: A conversational assistant that fetches and summarises live global news rather than relying on stale training data. Built as a LangGraph StateGraph agent loop (agent decides if news is needed, calls the Currents API tool, then summarises) with a MemorySaver checkpointer keeping conversation memory per session. Summaries link back to original articles.

agents.title: Fridge to Dinner
agents.description: An AI kitchen assistant that finds real recipes from ingredients you already have, ranked by fewest missing items. Built as a LangChain tool-calling agent with two tools (search by ingredients, fetch recipe details) backed by the Spoonacular API, so it grounds every suggestion in real data and never invents a recipe from memory.

agents.title: LangChain Weather Agent
agents.description: A conversational weather assistant built on LangChain's create_agent tool-calling loop, with separate tools for current conditions and a five-day forecast via the OpenWeather API. Built primarily to explore tool-calling mechanics, and the most useful lesson was that how you shape tool output affects the model's answer more than prompt wording does.

applied.title: UK Weather Mapping
applied.description: A live geospatial view of UK weather: pulls real-time conditions for 30+ cities from the OpenWeatherMap API, then renders them two ways. Static Cartopy maps cover temperature, conditions, and combined rainfall and wind, while an interactive Folium map adds clustered, pop-up-rich city markers. Built with retry-resilient request handling and written up end-to-end in an accompanying report.

applied.title: T2DM Urinary Metabolomics Analysis
applied.description: An NMR-based urinary metabolomics pipeline investigating biomarkers of Type 2 Diabetes: 220 spectral features across 132 samples (MetaboLights MTBLS1), analysed with a metabolome-wide association study (87 of 220 metabolites significant after FDR correction) and a cross-validated Random Forest classifier reaching AUC = 0.985 ± 0.022. Thirteen metabolites, including isoleucine, hippurate, and 2-oxoisovalerate, were confirmed by both methods.

applied.title: Solar Power Forecasting from Multi-Site Sensor Data
applied.description: Built and compared deep learning models (MLP, RNN, LSTM) to forecast short-term solar power output using weather and sensor data from 21 photovoltaic sites across Germany. Used sliding-window approaches and feature extraction (PCA, 1D CNN, autoencoders) to condense large time-series datasets, with deep models showing consistent gains over standard ML baselines.
